html:
The In-SHUCK-ch are a small group of First Nations on the lower Lillooet River, south of Pemberton in British Columbia. They are also called the Lower Lillooet people, part of the St'át'imc, and speak an Interior Salish language.

They fished for salmon, hunted and gathered in the narrow valley between Harrison Lake and Lillooet Lake, and traded with the Lil'wat upriver and the Stó:lō downriver.

In 1858 the Fraser Canyon Gold Rush turned their valley into a highway: the Douglas Road, a wagon and boat route to the gold fields, ran right through it. When other routes opened a few years later, traffic left the valley again, but settlers and logging stayed.
